title: NY State Senate · District 25
area: Central Brooklyn, including Bedford-Stuyvesant, Clinton Hill, Fort Greene, Prospect Heights, Ocean Hill and Brownsville.

context.text: Incumbent Jabari Brisport defeated Marlon Rice 78.3% to 21.3% (22,779 to 6,204 votes) in the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary. No Republican or other candidate is on the November 3 general-election ballot; Brisport, who also holds the Working Families Party line, is running unopposed.

summary.text: Jabari Brisport is the Democratic and Working Families Party incumbent for District 25 in central Brooklyn, running unopposed in the general election. A former public school math teacher and self-described democratic socialist, he chairs the Senate Children and Families Committee and has focused on child care, housing, and immigrant rights.

background.text: Born in Bedford-Stuyvesant and raised in Prospect Heights, Brooklyn; describes himself as the son of an undocumented immigrant.
Earned a bachelor's degree from New York University in 2009 and a master's degree from Yale University in 2014.
Worked as a public school math teacher in Crown Heights and was an active member of the United Federation of Teachers before his election.
Was an organizer for same-sex marriage legalization in New York (2009-2011) and an early organizer with the Black Lives Matter movement.

priorities.text: Campaign platform lists winning universal child care, building affordable housing, and "fighting Trump and ICE out of NYC" as top priorities.
priorities.quote: Winning Universal Child Care Building Affordable Housing Fighting Trump and ICE Out of NYC

priorities.text: As Children and Families Committee chair, says he has led the fight for universal child care and helped secure $1.4 billion in public school funding.
priorities.quote: As chair of the Children & Families Committee, I have led the fight for universal child care and helped secure $1.4B to fund our public schools, passed the Build Public Renewables Act to help fund green schools, and enacted protections for homeless youth.

priorities.text: Says he will continue fighting for fully funded public housing and against privatization of NYCHA, including RAD/PACT conversions.
priorities.quote: I will continue to fight for fully funded public housing and against all forms of privatization of NYCHA, including the RAD/PACT conversions – it is what is owed to our public housing tenants.

positions.summary: Lists winning universal child care as a top campaign priority and cites his record as Children and Families Committee chair on the issue.
Campaign platform calls for rent control and affordable housing and opposes privatization of public housing.
Campaign platform pledges to fight federal immigration enforcement ("ICE") activity in New York City and defend immigrants' civil rights.
Cites passage of the Build Public Renewables Act, which expands public renewable-energy development, as part of his legislative record.

record.text: Sponsored S10000, which lets foster youth 18 or older at their permanency hearing request confidentiality protections over notices and reports; passed the Senate 47-13 on May 28, 2026 and was on the Assembly floor calendar as of this research.
Sponsored S9814, which would extend paid sick leave protections to app-based delivery workers; referred to the Senate Labor Committee on April 6, 2026.
Sponsored S9813, which would classify app-based delivery workers as employees entitled to workers' compensation coverage; referred to the Senate Labor Committee on April 6, 2026.
Chairs the Senate Children and Families Committee; also serves on the Banks, Codes, Housing Construction and Community Development, and Libraries committees.
